technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Cloud Stream as the abstraction layer for message bus and Kafka integration.
For Kafka source offset control, persist consumer offsets in an external state store (e.g., Redis) to survive crashes.
Pre-allocation of partitions for Kafka sources will use static partition assignment, disabling automatic rebalancing.
For pre-allocation between nodes in the message bus, extend the stream deployment logic to assign partitions at deployment time.
Reactor-stream module will be implemented using Project Reactor, supporting time-window operations with configurable expressions.
Microbatching capability will be implemented by adding a batchInterval property to source modules, buffering events and flushing at intervals.
Performance testing infrastructure will use Rackspace cloud VMs with Kafka, monitoring tools, and automated benchmark scripts.
assumptions: Developer is proficient in Java 17, Spring Framework 6.0, Kafka, Project Reactor, and the existing Spring XD codebase.
Existing Spring XD codebase is modular and well-tested, requiring only incremental changes.
All source and sink modules already exist except for the new reactor-stream processor and microbatching modifications.
The state store for Kafka offsets (e.g., Redis) is already available or easy to set up in the development environment.
Documentation will be created in a wiki (e.g., Confluence) and will cover all new modules and features.
Performance testing infrastructure setup on Rackspace can be done manually without automating provisioning.
Effort estimates are for a single developer working full-time on all activities.
No significant architectural refactoring is required beyond the specified features.

activities.activity_description: Implement pre-allocation of partitions between nodes for the message bus, ensuring stable assignment across containers.

Implement reactor-stream processor module with time-window operations, support for expressions (min, avg, etc.), and integration with XD DSL.

Provision Rackspace VMs, install Kafka, monitoring tools, configure benchmark scripts, and verify baseline performance.
